这里真正值得担心的是收入和成本的时间差。招股书也提醒，公司的收入主要按照实际使用量计费，很多收入并没有对应的长期合同保障。但算力和基础设施的付款承诺可能持续多年。简单说，客户今天愿意大量使用Claude，公司收入就很好看，但如果明年AI需求降温，客户减少使用量，收入可能放缓，可已经签下的算力合同和租赁账单不会自动消失。

evidence.quote: TEEs exist to make zero data retention a verifiable proof, not a promise. This fall an attacker could read requests on one of our inference servers and took the root key of our legacy KMS.

In late October, an experimental DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 server took live OpenRouter traffic without attestation checks. An attacker got into it, and from Oct 21 to Nov 1 could read the request bodies passing through. On Nov 5 the same attacker reached Phala Cloud. The allowlist check on our legacy KMS had been turned off, so it released its root key to code

If you run a Phala Cloud app deployed before Nov 6 that uses getKey(), you need to move what those keys protect to new keys. Redeploying won't fix this, because the attacker still holds a copy of the old root key. If you sent requests to that DeepSeek route in that window, please treat anything in them as exposed and rotate it. If you self-host dstack, you

We've emailed every affected Phala Cloud team, and OpenRouter has notified affected inference users. Emails get missed, so we're saying it here too. (On-chain KMS users, apps deployed after Nov 6, all other OpenRouter traffic, and direct inference customers are unaffected.)

This is difficult to quantify although we know that frontier labs are extremely incentivized to drive this and there are signs that AI models

items.event: IoTeX 研究人员完成 McEliece 小参数挑战
items.new_information: 给出公开挑战的实际计算成本，并明确结果不适用于现实部署的参数。

evidence.quote: Our co-founder @Raullen and cryptographer @cryptoxfan just pushed the frontier of post-quantum cryptanalysis. Here's what that means, in plain English.

To find out how strong McEliece really is, the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) published a public ladder of puzzles: smaller versions of McEliece, from easy to very hard. Solve one, and you've recovered a private key from nothing but the public key.

They solved five of them, including three that no one had ever publicly solved before. The toughest of the five, TII-185, meant breaking through a technical ceiling that previous methods couldn't get past.

The most striking part is the cost. One puzzle that took a cluster of thousands of CPU cores nearly an hour, they solved in 19 minutes on 8 rented GPUs, for about $4.30. That's 3x faster, on hardware anyone can rent.
To be clear: this does not break McEliece as actually used. Real-world parameters are far, far bigger than these puzzles. This is exactly the kind of stress test that keeps those margins honest.

evidence.quote: Update from @yukonresearch on resolving P-vs-NP
The circuit lower bound on boolean circuits has moved beyond 5n just now. This is high-frequency research at its best.

To recap, this challenge is about the long standing open problem of circuit lower bound on Boolean circuits. The statement is to come up with an explicit family of Boolean functions in NP, one for each input length of n bits, and prove that every circuit constructed from two-input logic gates to compute it needs at least c·n^p gates, for all large n, with c
The power p is still 1 but there has been rapid progress in the coefficient c in last one month. You can see the timeline of progress below.

The big picture implication of this circuit lower bound problem is that if someone were to be able to come up with an explicit family of Boolean functions that has lower bound grow faster than every polynomial, that will prove P not equal to NP.

We collaborated with legendary cryptographer Amit Sahai to bring this problem of circuit lower bound to @yukonresearch in order to have open multiplayer format make progress on it. All progress in CircuitBreaker challenge are LLM-verified till now, expect to have human expert review soon.
